newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on wheat, supplies.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on wheat, supplies.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a drop in wheat futures plus the large supply of feedgrains worldwide, traders said.
South Korean buyers are expected to be in the market soon for 100,000 tonnes of feed wheat, traders in Seoul said over the weekend.
U.S. traders said corn continued to be burdened by USDA's recent crop report which showed U.S. 1996 corn production prospects well above average analysts' estimates.
Increased sorghum production in the United States also was cited along with the ready supply of feed wheat.
Bear spreading also was noted with E.D. and F. Man International a featured spreader of five million bushels of March/December, traders said.
Cargill Inc bought six million bushels of March and sold two million December, traders said, and Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought three million December and sold two million March.
Refco Inc sold two million bushels of March, Dean Witter Reynolds sold one million March and Iowa Grain sold one million bushels of March, traders said.
Corn closed 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower to one cent higher, with December down 3-1/2 at $2.66 a bushel.
Corn futures dropped despite an impressive rally in soybeans plus a stronger-than-expected number for U.S. corn export inspections.
USDA Monday said U.S. corn inspected for export during the week ended November 14 totaled 55.791 million bushels, well above trade expectations for 38 million to 46 million bushels.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 57,000 contracts, down from 69,244 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Griffin Trading bought 1,000 March $2.60 puts at 5-1/4 cents, Cargill Investor Services bought 500 July $3.50 calls and sold 500 July $4.00 calls at 1-3/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, up from 16,542 Friday.
